title: Telangana Assembly Erupts as Speaker Breaks Down Over Alleged Caste Slurs by BRS Lawmaker
excerpt: BRS MLC Tata Madhu was arrested for allegedly using derogatory language against Dalit Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar during a protest outside the Assembly, with CM Revanth Reddy calling it a "dark day for Telangana."
body:
• Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar broke down in the House after BRS MLC Tata Madhu allegedly made derogatory, caste-based remarks against him during a protest.
  • BRS leaders including KTR and Harish Rao were detained by police after a confrontation at the Assembly gate, where legislators wearing black outfits clashed with security.
  • CM Revanth Reddy termed the incident a "dark day for Telangana" and demanded the MLC's dismissal, with ministers calling for charges under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act.
  • The BRS has denied the allegations, with the MLC claiming his remarks were directed at police personnel, not the Speaker.

Emotional Scenes in the Assembly

Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar became visibly emotional and broke down in the House on Monday after the ruling Congress party raised allegations of verbal abuse by a Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) lawmaker.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2097176084588441721

The flashpoint came when Minister for Panchayat Raj Seethakka condemned remarks allegedly made by BRS MLC Tata Madhu during a heated protest outside the Assembly building earlier in the day. As details of the alleged slurs were discussed, Speaker Gaddam Prasad — who belongs to the Dalit community — was overcome with emotion.

Chaos at the Assembly Gate

The day's events began with BRS legislators arriving at the Assembly wearing black outfits with anti-government slogans. A confrontation erupted at the gate when security personnel denied them entry, leading to a physical scuffle between the opposition members and police.

During the commotion, MLC Tata Madhu allegedly made objectionable and caste-based remarks directed at the Speaker. Police subsequently detained several senior BRS leaders, including KT Rama Rao (KTR) and former minister T. Harish Rao, shifting them to local police stations. Tata Madhu and another MLC, Naveen Kumar Reddy, were arrested.

"This is a dark day for Telangana and an insult to the 40 million people of Telangana. Their leader provoked them to behave in this manner and sent them here. They attacked the police system and insulted the Speaker using such inappropriate language."

— A. Revanth Reddy, Chief Minister of Telangana

Caste Dimension Sharpens the Debate

The ruling Congress party framed the incident squarely as caste discrimination. Minister Seethakka alleged that the BRS leadership's hostility toward Speaker Gaddam Prasad stems from his Dalit identity, calling former CM K. Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR) the "ambassador of bad language."

Multiple ministers demanded that charges be filed against Tata Madhu under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Labour Minister G. Vivek Venkataswamy went further, stating the remarks were "not directed at just one individual — they were words spoken against the entire Dalit community."

CM Revanth Reddy demanded a public apology from KCR and called for Tata Madhu's dismissal from the Legislative Council, saying the office of the Speaker carries the highest stature in the House and must be respected regardless of political disagreements.

BRS Denies the Allegations

The BRS has pushed back against the accusations. Tata Madhu clarified that his contentious remarks were directed at police personnel during the scuffle, not at the Assembly Speaker. The party characterized the incident as an overreaction by the ruling government and pointed to alleged police heavy-handedness during the protest.

Opposition members also approached the High Court, seeking action against what they described as mistreatment by police during the demonstration. The BJP, AIMIM, and CPI all condemned the language allegedly used against the Speaker.

Democratic Norms Under Strain

For the Indian diaspora, the episode is a stark reminder of the caste fault lines that continue to shape Indian politics. The targeting of a constitutional officeholder with alleged caste slurs strikes at the foundations of democratic governance — an institution that NRIs frequently cite as India's defining strength.

The incident also reflects the deepening hostility between the Congress and BRS in Telangana since the 2023 change of government, a rivalry that shows no signs of cooling as both parties jockey for dominance in the state's political landscape.
